version_guard: Exact 20-column header (rank … combined_timeouts_zero); every row states a harness in {Codex, Claude Code}, an effort in {low, medium, high, extra-high, max} and a protocol in exactly {code-quality-maintenance-v3.4, code-quality-maintenance-v3.5, code-quality-maintenance-v3.6, code-quality-maintenance-v3.7, code-quality-maintenance-v3.15, code-quality-maintenance-v3.16, code-quality-maintenance-v3.17, code-quality-maintenance-v3.18, code-quality-maintenance-v3.23, code-quality-maintenance-v3.24, code-quality-maintenance-v3.29}. Any other protocol revision is unapproved and fails closed until its own published judge-protocols.json shows this family’s invariants — an amendment chain over the reviewed revisions and an identical rubric, system prompt, instructions, weights, gate allowance, repeats, seed, control-source hashes and scored panel — and its per-run export the same 23 task ids, or until it is given a separate version identity. A different task count, column set, protocol family or renamed suite is a different identity and fails closed; a column appended to the reviewed header quarantines this arm until that column is reviewed into this sentence. The board itself publishes and ranks its disclosed short rows (the board’s 2026-09-19 update: GPT-5.6 Sol at max, 22 of 23); only Benchmark Heaven’s comparison treats them differently, keyed on the board’s own passed_of and combined_timeouts_zero. Every row Benchmark Heaven compares carries a combined score over the full 23 tasks: where passed_of is below 23 the board scored the row over a smaller set and no such figure exists, so the row is withheld; where passed_of is 23 and n is lower, the row ran all 23 and the board publishes the combined score over all of them, each unfinished run scored 0, in combined_timeouts_zero — that is the figure we publish, never the headline combined_33 over the judged runs alone. combined_timeouts_zero must equal combined_33 × n ÷ passed_of wherever the board populates it; more than three withheld rows, any passed_of outside 1..23, or any n outside 1..passed_of fails closed. Review 2026-10-07: the exact Grok 4.7 / Cursor / code-quality-maintenance-v3.20 / benchmarks/swe-v4-grok47-cursor-v320.html population is excluded (how_to_collect.excluded_rows), not admitted to this protocol list. https://vulcanbench.com/leaderboard.html states that GPT-6.1 Sol replaces Grok 4.6 as judge and its scores are “not strictly comparable with the other columns”. Cursor is a stated source harness for that excluded population only; any other Cursor population fails closed. Excluded rows retain model, effort and harness in rejection evidence and never become a Codex or Claude Code observation. Review 2026-10-14: v3.24 amends v3.23 and preserves the listed invariants and task set. Its 38-column per-run export is a separate evidence file; the board CSV remains the exact 20-column collector input.

scoring.metric: Combined score across the 23 tasks, one column per model × reasoning-effort level: 100 × (0.50 × partial-credit functional hidden-test score + 0.085 × lint/complexity (ruff, radon) + 0.085 × security static analysis + 0.33 × judged Code quality), averaged over the runs of that column
scoring.notes: Published and maintained by Morgan Linton on vulcanbench.com; the leaderboard renders assets/data/swe-v4-board.csv (20 columns, one row per model × effort), and the board publishes and ranks every row it measures. Two columns state a row’s coverage: passed_of is the task set the row was scored over, and n is how many of those runs were judged. Where they differ the board also publishes combined_timeouts_zero, its combined score over all 23 runs with each unfinished run scored 0 — the figure its own footnote gives as 71.94 at extra-high and 67.26 at max for GPT-6 Luna, and the one its best-effort tag uses. It equals combined_33 × n ÷ passed_of on every row that carries it. The board’s footnotes disclose both kinds of short row: GPT-5.6 Sol at max and Opus 5.5 at high were scored over 22 tasks, while GPT-6 Luna at max and extra-high ran all 23 and did not finish every run. Each column aggregates every run of that model at that effort level in its own agent harness (Codex on a ChatGPT subscription, or Claude Code); Fable 5.1’s runs include 11 disclosed Opus 4.8 fallback cells that the operator keeps in the population (source footnote). Code quality is judged for a human reader by Muse Spark 1.3 and Grok 4.6 under one frozen protocol family; the reviewed set is exactly code-quality-maintenance-v3.4, v3.5, v3.6, v3.7, v3.15, v3.16, v3.17, v3.18, v3.23, v3.24 and v3.29. The board states of the first four that "v3.4 to v3.7 apply the same rubric, controls, gates and judges to each population". v3.15 — the Claude Opus 5.5 population published 2026-09-26 — is the same family on its own published evidence bundle (D223, 2026-09-27): its judge-protocols.json amends v3…v3.7 and carries a byte-identical rubric, system prompt, pair/probe/match instructions, weights, gate allowance, repeats, seed, judge control-source hashes and scored panel (Muse Spark 1.3 at medium, Cursor Grok 4.6 Medium) to the v3.4/v3.5/v3.6/v3.7 bundles, and its per-run export covers the same 23 task ids as the v3.4 export. v3.16 — the GPT-6 Luna population — is the same family on its own published evidence bundle (D256.1, 2026-09-29): its judge-protocols.json amends v3…v3.7 and v3.15 and carries a byte-identical rubric, system prompt, pair/probe/match instructions, weights, gate allowance, repeats, seed, judge control-source hashes and scored panel to the v3.4 bundle, and its per-run export covers the same 23 task ids in 115 rows (23 task ids × 5 effort levels). What differs between revisions is the population itself — the population record, the revision ids and hashes, the amendment chain, and the operator’s per-population handling notes (the single invalid-response retry disclosed from v3.7 on, v3.6’s judged top-up, a revision’s unpublished or not-judged runs). Inside this family every revision has its own protocol_sha256 — the accepted v3.4 rows even pair a v3.4 Muse protocol with a v3.3 Grok one — so a distinct revision hash is the family’s norm and not a break in it: the number tracks the amendment chain, not the rubric. The operator’s v3.8 and v3.14 revisions belong to its separate Routine board ("Compare levels and models within this table, never across the two boards") and are never mixed into this one. The operator discloses one harness confound between the two Claude columns: Opus 5.5 ran on Claude Code 2.1.280, Fable 5.1 on 2.1.259–2.1.261. The retired v3 suite is a different task set and scale, never comparable. The suite was renamed VulcanBench Frontier v4 (formerly VulcanBench-SWE v4, September 2026) with task set and report URLs unchanged. Review 2026-10-07 (https://vulcanbench.com/leaderboard.html, Frontier paragraph and ◊/‖/* footnotes): v3.17 and v3.18 retain the same rubric, controls, gates and judges. Their published judge-protocols.json bundles (assets/data/swe-v4-gpt6-sol-v317/ and assets/data/swe-v4-gpt61-sol-v318/ in https://github.com/morganlinton/VulcanBenchCOM) match every reviewed invariant against v3.4, including scored_panel, and their runs.csv exports each cover the same 23 task ids in 115 rows. The v3.17 medium row has n=22, passed_of=23 and no combined_timeouts_zero, so it remains withheld under the existing full-denominator rule; v3.18 scores one disclosed run from one valid judge under the unchanged single_panel_rule. Cursor agent CLI 2026.10.01 is explicitly stated for Grok 4.7, but v3.20 changes scored_panel to Muse Spark 1.3 and GPT-6.1 Sol. The source warns “its Code quality and combined score are not strictly comparable with the other columns”; that population is explicitly excluded, with no score or catalog join, pending a separate version identity. Source bytes, hashes and retrieval times for this review are retained in test/fixtures/vulcanbench-frontier-2026-10-07/manifest.json. Review 2026-10-10 (https://vulcanbench.com/leaderboard.html, Frontier paragraph and its †† footnote; report https://vulcanbench.com/benchmarks/swe-v4-sonnet55-v323.html): v3.23 — the Claude Sonnet 5.5 population, 115 runs (23 task ids × 5 effort levels) through Claude Code 2.1.291–2.1.293 — is the same family on its own published evidence bundle (assets/data/swe-v4-sonnet55-v323/ in https://github.com/morganlinton/VulcanBenchCOM). Its judge-protocols.json declares the amendment chain over the reviewed revisions v3…v3.15 and carries a byte-identical rubric, system prompt, pair/probe/match instructions, weights, gate allowance, repeats, seed, judge control-source hashes and scored panel (Muse Spark 1.3 at medium, Cursor Grok 4.6 Medium) to the reviewed v3.18 bundle, and its per-run export covers the same 23 task ids in 115 rows. The board itself keeps v3.23 in this family — “v3.4 to v3.7, v3.15 to v3.18, v3.20 and v3.23 apply the same rubric, controls and gates to each population” — and the report states the revision changes nothing in the rubric, controls, quirk keys, gates, repeats, seed, weights or judge settings. The board discloses two population facts that stay disclosures, not guard changes: Grok 4.6 judged through the self-updating Cursor CLI 2026.10.01-e373342 (the v3.3 round recorded 2026.09.02-c22c1a3) with the same pinned model id and a passed v3.23 calibration exam, and the solver sweep predates the harness’s 2026-10-05 tagged-worktree rule, so its task content was admitted through a committed hash bridge (task_hash_bridge, 23 tasks, sha256 544f591c…) after every agent-visible cached .pyc proved byte-identical to compiling the starting source; Claude Code’s refusal fallback stayed on and the board states “no reply came from another model”. All five Sonnet 5.5 rows carry n=23 and passed_of=23 and publish at combined_33. Source bytes, hashes and retrieval times for this review are retained in test/fixtures/vulcanbench-frontier-2026-10-10/manifest.json. Review 2026-10-14 (https://vulcanbench.com/leaderboard.html and https://vulcanbench.com/benchmarks/swe-v4-haiku55-v324.html): v3.24 is the Haiku 5.5 population, 115 runs across the same 23 tasks at five effort levels. Its judge-protocols.json amends v3.23 and is identical on the rubric, system, pair/probe/match instructions, schemas, weights, gates, repeats, seed, single-panel rule, retry rule, control-source hashes and scored panel; Muse uses the same binary and Grok the same pinned Cursor CLI version. Both judges passed 80-call calibration with no allowance. The per-run export independently confirms the same 23 task ids in 115 rows. Its 38-column export is separate from the collector input: the main board CSV still has the guarded 20-column header. The report discloses four unscored runs (three safety stops and one invalid Grok probe) and one excerpt re-wrap recovery; the published wrapper requires exact source text after whitespace/line-break collapse, records the original and leaves the score unchanged. The board has five v3.24 Haiku rows; Low and High have n=23, while Medium, Extra-high and Max have fewer judged runs and no combined_timeouts_zero, so those three remain withheld under the existing full-denominator rule. Source bytes, hashes and retrieval times are retained in test/fixtures/vulcanbench-frontier-2026-10-14/manifest.json. Review 2026-10-31 (https://vulcanbench.com/leaderboard.html and https://vulcanbench.com/benchmarks/swe-v4-gpt61-terra-v329.html): v3.29 is the GPT-6.1 Terra population (Codex CLI 0.159.0), 115 runs across the same 23 tasks at five effort levels, judged by Muse Spark 1.3 and Grok 4.6. Its report states “Protocol v3.29 changes nothing in the rubric, controls, quirk keys, gates, repeats, seed, weights or judges from v3.24”, and its judge-protocols.json amends v3.24 and is identical on the rubric, system, pair/probe/match instructions, schemas, weights, gates, repeats, seed, single-panel rule, retry rule, control-source hashes and scored panel; Muse uses the same binary (the bundle’s same_as_v324 record) and Grok the Cursor CLI version and digest v3.24 pinned (2026.10.01-e373342), judged through that version’s own launcher although Cursor has since updated itself. Both judges passed 80-call calibration; Muse missed one gate (g11_repeatability), inside the frozen gate_allowance (max_failing_gates 1, unchanged from v3.24). The per-run export independently confirms the same 23 task ids in 115 rows, every cell judged on 23 runs. One probe recovery is disclosed: Muse’s intent probe of max settlecore quoted a byte-string line with its escapes decoded, recovered under the v3.18 wrapper rule recover_escaped_excerpts, which the owner extended (2026-10-29) to the source’s backslash-x-00 spelling of NUL; the rule only writes the quoted excerpt back as the code spells it, and the published wrapper records the original. The main board CSV keeps the guarded 20-column header. All five v3.29 rows carry n=23 and passed_of=23 and publish at combined_33. The board now also carries v3.26 (Muse Wonder Full, judged by Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol), v3.27 (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash) and v3.28 (Reflection Beam); v3.27 and v3.28 are judged by Muse Spark 1.3 and GPT-6.1 Sol. None is judged by the Muse Spark 1.3 and Grok 4.6 panel; the board’s footnotes call v3.26 and v3.27 not strictly comparable with the other columns and state that GPT-6.1 Sol rates v3.28’s reviewed Code quality about 14 points above Muse, so, like v3.20, their rows are excluded rejection evidence (how_to_collect.excluded_rows) and would need their own judge-panel version identity. Source bytes, hashes and retrieval times are retained in test/fixtures/vulcanbench-frontier-2026-10-31/manifest.json.

description: 23 behavioural-reconstruction tasks: the model must repair a replacement implementation of a legacy program until hidden tests confirm it reproduces the program’s real drift from its written spec; the combined score weights functional correctness 50%, lint/complexity 8.5%, security 8.5% and judged Code quality 33%.
